look_here_first: LOOK HERE FIRST: Inspect the head: outer sterile florets are enlarged and trumpet-like with fringed tips, surrounding shorter central fertile florets. Then turn the head sideways to inspect several rows of non-spiny green phyllaries with dark or pale papery fringed appendages. Check the narrow alternate leaves and slightly woolly stems; blue color alone is not a reliable ID.

key_traits.label: Habit
key_traits.text: Annual herb, typically upright with slender branches, often woolly when young.

key_traits.label: Leaves attachment
key_traits.text: Alternate narrow linear to lanceolate leaves, usually sessile on upper stem; lower leaves can be sparsely toothed or lobed; white woolly hairs may be visible.

key_traits.label: Flower reproductive
key_traits.text: Heads at branch ends; enlarged, usually blue but variable-colored outer sterile florets surround smaller fertile florets. The bell-shaped involucre has multiple rows of green phyllaries with scarious fringed tips, often brown to dark.

key_traits.label: Fruit seed
key_traits.text: Small pale-to-gray cypselae with a short tuft of stiff pappus bristles; needs exact-species macro.

key_traits.label: Stem bud
key_traits.text: Slender non-winged stems with woolly hairs; check attachment of upper leaves.
